 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Periya Nayagam in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 23.04.2024 at about 8.50 p.m. Periya Nayagam was pushing the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-53-K-4772, on NH-44 road, near Setdine, infront of Bharat Hotel Chikkaballapur, at that time, driver of Canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R-4479 came with high speed in a rash and negligent and dashed against the deceased motor cycle.
Due to said impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Chikkaballapura, thereafter shifted to NIMHANS and later admitted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, inspite of best treatment, the deceased succumbed to injuries.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale, healthy, aged about 43 years and Crane Operator and driver by earning Rs.30,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark, causing lot of pain, shock and mental agony.
4. It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R-4479.

In this regard,
Chikkaballapura Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of the Canter in Crime No.74/2024 for the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, this petition.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before this court,
remained absent, placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R-4479 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
It is also contention of the respondent that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.

Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive,
exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Periya Nayagam died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 23.04.2024 at about 5.50 p.m. near Set Dinne, infront of Bharat Hotel, Chikkaballapura, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Canter bearing registration No.TN-77- R-4479 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

If so, at what rate ? From whom?
4) What order or award?
8.
In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P18.

12.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R- 4479, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Periya Nayagam died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

13. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the Canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R-4479,
14.

On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the rider of the offending vehicle in question.
15. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Perianayagammal examined as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Thoma Ambose, the S.H.O. of Chikkaballapura circle police have registered the case against the driver of the Canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R-4479 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of I.P.C.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the Canter alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.

18. Though, the respondent No.2 has examined ASI, Chikkaballapura Rural Police as RW1.
He has placed charge sheet, for alteration of vehicle number requisition letter and order sheet in CC 1052/2024 at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
But his evidence will not much helpful to disprove the case of the petitioner.
19. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Canter bearing No.TN-77-R-4479 and in the said accident, Periya Nayagam succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly,
I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 and 3:
20.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P12 to Ex.P18 i.e., Driving Licence, Ration Card,
Aadhar cards and Pan card of the deceased have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

21. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 & 3 are children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of the deceased, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
22. The petitioners herein, have placed driving licence, which is marked at Ex.P12 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 22.9.1979.
The accident occurred on 23.04.2024.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 45 years.

For his age, multiplier '14' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
23.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was running Crane Operator & Driver and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.

Hence,
in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per Perianayagammal vs Mowri Enterprises on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144061134/
5 law.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2024.

By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- for the year 2024.
24.
Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

25. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
26. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are four persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
27. In the present case, deceased was aged about 45 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "14" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was under the purview of 40-50 years, 25% of the income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,98,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,98,000+49,500) = Rs.2,47,500/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,65,000/-
(Rs.2,47,500-Rs.82,500).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "14" which comes to Rs.23,10,000/-.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

29. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.18,150/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also

by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.48,400/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter bearing registration No.TN-77-R-4479, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
33. As per records, insurance policy was valid from 1.09.2023 to 31.08.2024.
The alleged accident had taken place on 23.04.2024.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Hence,
respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative and issue No.3 is partly Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
34.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,91,500/- (Rupees twenty four lakhs ninety one thousand and five hundred only), from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 60% and the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled the share of 20% each.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 2, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of his choice till he attains age of majority,
after attaining the age of majority entire amount shall be released to him through due process of law.
The guardian of the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
